lessons.title: Introduction to CSS

content.title: What is CSS?
content.text: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It is used to control the appearance, layout and presentation of HTML elements.

content.title: CSS Rule
content.text: A CSS rule normally contains a selector followed by declarations. Each declaration contains a property and a value.

content.title: Ways to Add CSS
content.text: CSS can be written inline, inside a style element, or in an external stylesheet. External stylesheets are commonly preferred for maintainability.

key_points: Values define how the property is applied.

lessons.title: Selectors and Colors

content.title: Element Selector
content.text: An element selector targets all elements of a particular HTML type.

content.title: Class Selector
content.text: A class selector begins with a dot and targets elements having the specified class.

content.title: ID Selector
content.text: An ID selector begins with # and targets an element with the specified ID.

content.title: Colors
content.text: CSS colors can be specified using names, hexadecimal values, RGB, RGBA and other supported formats.

key_points: Class selectors begin with a dot.

content.title: Font Properties
content.text: CSS provides properties such as font-family, font-size, font-weight and font-style for controlling text appearance.

content.title: Font Styling
Text Alignment
content.text: The text-align property can align text to the left, right, center or justify.

content.title: Backgrounds
content.text: Background properties control the background color or image of an element.

lessons.title: The CSS Box Model

content.title: Box Model
content.text: Every HTML element can be considered as a rectangular box consisting of content, padding, border and margin.

content.title: Box Model
Padding
content.text: Padding creates space between an element's content and its border.

content.title: Margin
content.text: Margin creates space outside an element's border.

content.title: Border
content.text: A border surrounds the padding and content area.

key_points: The box model consists of content, padding, border and margin.
box-sizing can change how dimensions are calculated.

lessons.title: Positioning and Display

content.title: Display
content.text: The display property controls how an element participates in layout.

content.title: Display Values
Position
content.text: The position property controls how an element is positioned. Common values include static, relative, absolute, fixed and sticky.

content.title: Relative and Absolute

key_points: block elements normally occupy a full line.
inline elements normally occupy only their required space.

lessons.title: Flexbox

content.title: What is Flexbox?
content.text: Flexbox is a CSS layout system designed to arrange elements along a row or column.

content.title: Basic Flexbox
justify-content
content.text: justify-content controls how flex items are distributed along the main axis.

content.title: align-items
content.text: align-items controls how flex items are aligned along the cross axis.

content.title: Flex Direction
content.text: flex-direction controls whether items are arranged in a row or column.

key_points: display: flex creates a flex container.
flex-direction controls row or column arrangement.

lessons.title: CSS Grid

content.title: What is CSS Grid?
content.text: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system that allows elements to be arranged using rows and columns.

content.title: Grid Columns
content.text: grid-template-columns defines the number and size of columns.

content.title: Gap
content.text: The gap property controls spacing between grid items.

key_points: Grid is useful for two-dimensional layouts.
Grid can define rows and columns.
The gap property creates space between grid items.
fr represents a fraction of available space.

lessons.title: Responsive Design

content.title: Responsive Design
content.text: Responsive design allows a web page to adapt to different screen sizes such as phones, tablets and desktops.

content.title: Media Queries
content.text: Media queries apply CSS rules conditionally based on characteristics such as viewport width.

content.title: Responsive Layouts
content.text: Flexible widths, relative units, Flexbox, Grid and media queries can be combined to create responsive layouts.

content.title: CSS and HTML
content.text: HTML provides the structure while CSS controls presentation and layout. Keeping structure and styling separate makes applications easier to maintain.

key_points: Responsive design adapts to different screen sizes.
Flexbox and Grid are useful for responsive layouts.
HTML provides structure and CSS provides presentation.
